source_text: Ad hanc partem zelus fidei perora!bit ingemens: Christianum ab idolis in ecclesiam uenire, de aduersaria officina in domum dei uenire, attollere ad deum patrem manus matres idolorum, his manibus adorare, quae foris aduersus deum adorantur, eas manus admouere corpori domini, quae daemoniis corpora conferunt? nec hoc sufficit. parum sit, si ab aliis manibus accipiant quod contaminent, sed etiam. ipsae tradunt aliis quod contaminauerunt. adleguntur in ordinem ecclesiasticum artifices idolorum. pro scelus! semel Iudaei Christo manus intulerunt, isti quotidie corpus eius lacessunt. o manus praecidendae ! uiderint iam, an per similitudinem dictum sit: si te manus tua scandalizat, amputa eam. quae magis amputandae, quam in quibus domini corpus scandalizatur?
thought_title: The craftsman's hands defile the church
orientation: Tertullian is denouncing idol-making craftsmen who come into the Christian assembly and handle the Lord's body with the same hands that serve idols.
pass_a_gloss: Against this part the zeal of faith will plead, groaning: a Christian comes from idols into the church, comes from the workshop of the adversary into the house of God, lifts up to God the Father hands that are mothers of idols, worships with these hands which outside are worshipped against God, applies to the body of the Lord those hands which confer bodies to demons? And this is not enough. Let it be a small thing if they receive from other hands what they defile, but even they themselves hand over to others what they have defiled. Craftsmen of idols are chosen into the ecclesiastical order. O the crime! Once the Jews laid hands on Christ, these people daily assault his body. O hands that ought to be cut off! Let them see now whether it was said by way of comparison: if your hand scandalizes you, cut it off. Which hands ought more to be cut off than those in which the body of the Lord is scandalized?

choices.why: Keeps the striking metaphor: the hands give birth to idols by making them.
Concrete place of production, contrasting with the house of God.

choices.english: are chosen into the ecclesiastical order
choices.why: Renders the technical sense of enrollment into church office.
Preserves the exclamatory force and the noun scelus as a moral outrage.
Captures the aggressive, repeated provocation against Christ's body.
Renders the rhetorical figure Tertullian invokes for the saying.

bible_refs.note: si te manus tua scandalizat, amputa eam

pass_b_english: At this point the zeal of faith will plead with groans: a Christian comes from idols into the church, from the adversary's workshop into the house of God, and lifts up to God the Father hands that are mothers of idols. With those hands he worships, the very hands that outside are used to worship against God. He applies to the Lord's body the same hands that bestow bodies on demons. Nor is this enough. It would be a small thing if they only received from other hands what they defile, but they themselves hand on to others what they have defiled. Craftsmen of idols are chosen into the ecclesiastical order. O the crime! The Jews laid hands on Christ once; these men assault his body every day. O hands that ought to be cut off! Let them now consider whether it was said by way of comparison: if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off (Matthew 5:30). Which hands more deserve to be cut off than those in which the Lord's body is caused to stumble?

last_rejected.why: 'aduersaria' means 'opposing/hostile,' not 'the adversary's' (Satan's). It describes the workshop as hostile to God.
last_rejected.ruling: adversaria can mean hostile or 'of the adversary'; 'adversary's workshop' conveys the intended sense

problems.quote: worshipping with those hands that outside are worshipped against God
problems.why: Hands 'worshipped against God' is nonsensical; should be 'worship with'.
problems.fix: Change to 'with which idols are worshipped outside against God'.

edits.old: worshipping with those hands that outside are worshipped against God
edits.new: worshipping with those hands with which idols are worshipped outside against God

fixed: The English 'worshipping with those hands that outside are worshipped against God' misreads the source 'his manibus adorare, quae foris aduersus deum adorantur': the relative 'quae' refers to the idols, not the hands, so the hands are the instruments with which idols are worshipped, not the objects worshipped. Changed to 'worshipping with those hands with which idols are worshipped outside against God'.

polish.changed: Clarified the garbled sentence about hands and worship, made the subject of each action explicit, and smoothed the rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and quotation.
